key_insight: In simulated clinical prediction networks, reliable LLM auditing depended on computation tools and explicit instructions, not direct access to model weights.
clinical_relevance: Tool-assisted auditing may help identify prediction patterns and subgroup label bias, but clinical usefulness remains untested in real patient data.
method: Trained tanh networks with 105–38,401 weights on simulated subarachnoid haemorrhage cohorts with planted relationships, no relationship, or subgroup death under-recording.
Compared five GPT models using raw weights without tools versus calculation tools with weight access or prediction-only access.
Tested default versus explicit system instructions and compared LLM auditing and repair with a scripted approach.
evidence_signal: With tools, GPT-6 Astra recovered planted relationships in 29/29 runs, raised no false alarms in 15 null-network runs, and identified the biased subgroup in 6/6 runs; prediction-only access matched weight access.
watch_item: Results are limited to simulated cohorts and small networks, and a well-designed script matched comparator-model auditing and the best LLM repair.
paper_title: Computation, not weight access: large language models as auditors of clinical prediction networks
